question:
A student uses a simple microscope (magnifying glass) to read faint black text printed on glossy white paper under a lamp. Assume the microscope only increases the apparent angular size and does not change the relative intensities reaching the eye; hence the visibility is decided only by the intensities entering the eye.

The light reaching the eye from the white background region due to diffuse reflection is $I_w$ (unpolarized), and from the black text region due to diffuse reflection is $I_b$ (unpolarized), with $I_w=9I_b$.

In addition, specular glare from the glossy surface contributes an extra intensity $I_g=6I_b$ that is the same over both regions and is assumed to be completely linearly polarized (as for reflection near Brewster angle).

An ideal polarizer (analyzer) is placed just in front of the eye and oriented to minimize the glare (i.e., its transmission axis is perpendicular to the glare polarization, so the glare is ideally extinguished). The diffuse reflections from paper and ink remain unpolarized.

Define the Michelson contrast for viewing the text as

$C=\dfrac{I_{\max}-I_{\min}}{I_{\max}+I_{\min}},$

where $I_{\max}$ and $I_{\min}$ are the intensities reaching the eye from the white and black regions, respectively.

Find the contrast improvement factor $\dfrac{C_{\text{with polaroid}}}{C_{\text{without polaroid}}}$.
